--- title: "Replicating Cao & Dowd" subtitle: "The `cd` model against the paper, the authors' code, and mlsynth" --- The [`cd` model](../models/cd.qmd) is checked against three independent sources, each with the settings that source uses: 1. **The paper** (Cao & Dowd, arXiv:1902.07343v3), with scspill's default settings, which are the paper's Section 4 definitions. 2. **The authors' code** ([jcao0/synthetic-control-spillover](https://github.com/jcao0/synthetic-control-spillover) at commit `86004020`). Its Proposition 99 application output is checked with the application code's settings, and its simulation code's statistics are checked too. 3. **mlsynth's** `SPILLSYNTH(method="cd")`, an independent implementation of the same estimator, on frozen fixtures. The same checks run in the test suite (`scspill/tests/test_cd.py`, `test_cd_features.py`, `test_cd_mlsynth_parity.py`) and in the benchmark suite (`python benchmarks/run_benchmarks.py --case california_cd --case cd_vs_mlsynth`). This page runs them live. ::: {#1dc6e08f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import json from pathlib import Path import numpy as np import pandas as pd from scspill import SCSPILL from scspill.data import load_california_cd root = Path.cwd() while not (root / "benchmarks").exists(): # docs pages execute in docs/articles root = root.parent reference = root / "benchmarks" / "reference" APPLICATION_CODE = {"quantile_method": "linear", "ci_method": "published"} ``` ::: ## The paper Section 6.2 of v3 makes two checkable statements about the 51-unit Proposition 99 fit: - California's effects in 1989 and 1990 are not significantly different from zero at 5%, with intervals built by inverting the P test; - in Figure 3's sensitivity analysis, California's largest effect estimate meets the upper bound of the spillover-aware bias set at $\bar\alpha = 17.07$ with one missed spillover, and at $9.66$ with two. ::: {#1206b74b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit = SCSPILL({**load_california_cd(51).config_kwargs(), "display_graphs": False}).fit() fit.effect_ci["CA"].loc[[1989, 1990]].assign(estimate=fit.effects_panel["CA"]).round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
lower upper estimate
1989 -4.64 4.80 0.08
1990 -1.00 8.43 3.71
``` ::: ::: ::: {#ec4c5043 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} sens = fit.cd.sensitivity largest = fit.effects_panel["CA"].max() pd.Series( {f"p = {p}": round(largest / sens.coefficients(p)[0], 2) for p in (1, 2)}, name="break-even alpha_bar", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` p = 1 17.07 p = 2 9.66 Name: break-even alpha_bar, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ## The authors' application output The authors' Proposition 99 code uses two settings that differ from the paper: an interpolated quantile and signed-quantile intervals (see the [model page](../models/cd.qmd#departures)). With those two switches, scspill reproduces their frozen output for both specifications: ::: {#b98173f9 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = {} for spec in (51, 41): expected = json.loads((reference / "cao_dowd" / f"results_{spec}.json").read_text()) out = SCSPILL( {**load_california_cd(spec).config_kwargs(), **APPLICATION_CODE, "display_graphs": False} ).fit() effects = [out.effects_panel["CA"] - np.asarray(expected["te"])] p_equal = [np.array_equal(out.pointwise_p_values["CA"], expected["te_pvalue"])] for state in ("AZ", "NV", "OR"): effects.append(out.effects_panel[state] - np.asarray(expected["u" + state][19:])) p_equal.append(np.array_equal(out.pointwise_p_values[state], expected["p" + state])) rows[f"{spec} units"] = { "largest effect difference": float(np.abs(np.concatenate(effects)).max()), "largest counterfactual difference": float( np.abs(out.counterfactual - np.asarray(expected["sp"])).max() ), "every P value equal": all(p_equal), "condition number": round(out.cd.condition_number, 3), "authors' condition number": round(expected["cond"], 3), } pd.DataFrame(rows).T ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
largest effect difference largest counterfactual difference every P value equal condition number authors' condition number
51 units 0.0084 0.002502 True 12.485 12.485
41 units 0.004121 0.000785 True 4.341 4.341
``` ::: ::: Effects agree to within 0.01 packs per capita, and every P value matches exactly. The remaining gap is the simplex solver. With the authors' settings, SciPy's SLSQP stops short of the optimum for every unit of the 51-unit panel. scspill uses a scaled objective with analytic gradients and reaches an objective at or below theirs for every unit, so a few two-decimal values differ in the last digit. **The joint test of "no spillover anywhere".** The authors report it by year. The interpolated quantile reproduces their rejections, and the paper's left-inverse rule drops two of them: ::: {#058ca5f8 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} expected = json.loads((reference / "cao_dowd" / "results_51.json").read_text()) app = SCSPILL( {**load_california_cd(51).config_kwargs(), **APPLICATION_CODE, "display_graphs": False} ).fit() no_spillover = np.eye(len(app.unit_labels))[1:] pd.DataFrame( { "authors' output": expected["spillover_test"], "scspill, application code": [ int(app.test_hypothesis(no_spillover, period=t).reject) for t in app.effects_panel.index ], "scspill, paper (v3)": [ int(app.test_hypothesis(no_spillover, period=t, quantile_method="empirical").reject) for t in app.effects_panel.index ], }, index=app.effects_panel.index, ).T ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
1989 1990 1991 1992 1993 1994 1995 1996 1997 1998 1999 2000
authors' output 0 1 1 1 0 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
scspill, application code 0 1 1 1 0 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
scspill, paper (v3) 0 1 1 1 0 0 0 1 1 1 1 1
``` ::: ::: ## The authors' simulation code Three fixtures come from the authors' simulation code at the same commit: - the first replication of six simulation designs: stationary and integrated factors, at three distances of the pure donors; - all 50 leave-one-period-out reference statistics of one design; - the $\kappa_A$ statistics and references of a per-unit and a homogeneous structure. ::: {#9a1fcc7d .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} with np.load(reference / "cao_dowd" / "inference_replication_1.npz") as fixture: panels, estimates = fixture["panels"], fixture["sp_estimates"] labels = [f"U{i:02d}" for i in range(51)] def simulated(panel, **options): df = pd.DataFrame(panel, index=labels, columns=range(51)).stack().rename("y").reset_index() df.columns = ["unit", "time", "y"] df["treated"] = ((df["unit"] == "U00") & (df["time"] == 50)).astype(int) config = {"method": "cd", "df": df, "outcome": "y", "treat": "treated", "unitid": "unit", "time": "time", "affected_units": labels[1:14], "display_graphs": False} return SCSPILL({**config, **options}).fit() diffs = [abs(simulated(p).effects_panel.iloc[0, 0] - e) for p, e in zip(panels, estimates)] kappa = json.loads((reference / "cao_dowd" / "kappa_rep1.json").read_text()) homogeneous = simulated(panels[1], spillover_structure="homogeneous") loo = simulated(panels[1], reference_mode="leave_one_period_out") loo_ref = np.load(reference / "cao_dowd" / "loo_reference_stationary_r05_rep1.npy") pd.Series( { "largest effect difference, six designs": max(diffs), "largest leave-one-out reference difference": float( np.abs(loo.placebo_effects["U00"].to_numpy() ** 2 - loo_ref).max() ), "kappa_A difference, homogeneous": abs( homogeneous.kappa_test[50].statistic - kappa["homogeneous"]["statistic"] ), } ).map("{:.2e}".format).to_frame("difference from the authors' code") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
difference from the authors' code
largest effect difference, six designs 1.39e-05
largest leave-one-out reference difference 1.72e-04
kappa_A difference, homogeneous 7.15e-06
``` ::: ::: ## mlsynth mlsynth's `SPILLSYNTH(method="cd")` implements the same estimator with a different solver, cvxpy with CLARABEL. Its results on six cases are frozen in `benchmarks/reference/mlsynth_cd/` by `tools/freeze_mlsynth_cd_reference.py`: - the Proposition 99 panel under the per-unit, homogeneous and distance-decay structures; - a synthetic panel with two treated units, with and without efficient weighting. Under mlsynth's inference settings (those of the application code), scspill matches it: ::: {#d587a5c4 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} mls = json.loads((reference / "mlsynth_cd" / "reference.json").read_text()) def mlsynth_case(name, case): options = case["options"] if name.startswith("ca"): base = {**load_california_cd(int(name[2:4])).config_kwargs(), "affected_units": None} else: base = {"method": "cd", "df": pd.DataFrame(mls["panels"]["synth_two_treated"]), "outcome": "y", "treat": "treated", "unitid": "unit", "time": "time"} config = {**base, **APPLICATION_CODE, "display_graphs": False, "spillover_structure": options.get("spillover_structure", "per_unit")} for key in ("affected_units", "unit_distances"): if options.get(key) is not None: config[key] = options[key] if options.get("weighting", "identity") != "identity": config["weighting"] = options["weighting"] return SCSPILL(config).fit() rows = {} for name, case in mls["cases"].items(): out = mlsynth_case(name, case) units = case["units"] b = out.scm_matrix.loc[units, units].to_numpy() tests = {**case["treatment_tests"], **case["spillover_tests"]} rows[name] = { "largest B difference": float( np.abs(b - [[case["B"][u][v] for v in units] for u in units]).max() ), "largest effect difference": float( max(np.abs(out.effects_panel[u] - case["alpha"][u]).max() for u in units) ), "P values equal": all( np.array_equal(out.pointwise_p_values[u], t["p_value"]) for u, t in tests.items() ), } pd.DataFrame(rows).T ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
largest B difference largest effect difference P values equal
ca51_per_unit 0.000001 0.000019 True
ca41_per_unit 0.000006 0.000012 True
ca41_homogeneous 0.000006 0.000012 True
ca41_distance_decay 0.000006 0.000011 True
synth_two_treated 0.0 0.0 True
synth_efficient 0.0 0.0 True
``` ::: ::: **Structure selection.** mlsynth's `select_A_by_kappa` averages the per-period $\kappa_A$ norms. scspill offers that statistic as `statistic="mean_norm"`, and it reproduces mlsynth's choice. scspill's default is the paper's multi-period statistic (v3 Section S.1.3), which can rank the candidates differently: ::: {#dbfaa658 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} selection = mls["selection"] synthetic = SCSPILL( {"method": "cd", "df": pd.DataFrame(mls["panels"]["synth_homogeneous"]), "outcome": "y", "treat": "treated", "unitid": "unit", "time": "time", "affected_units": selection["candidates"]["per_unit_3"]["affected_units"], "display_graphs": False} ).fit() pd.DataFrame( { "mlsynth": selection["mean_kappa"], "scspill, mean_norm": synthetic.select_structure_by_kappa( selection["candidates"], statistic="mean_norm" ).statistics, "scspill, v3": synthetic.select_structure_by_kappa(selection["candidates"]).statistics, } ).round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}
mlsynth scspill, mean_norm scspill, v3
per_unit_3 1.617 1.617 1.085
homogeneous_3 2.001 2.001 1.306
per_unit_1 4.679 4.679 12.061
homogeneous_5 4.125 4.125 10.276
``` ::: ::: The provenance of every fixture (versions, commit, SHA-256 checksums) is recorded in `benchmarks/reference/cao_dowd/README.md` and `benchmarks/reference/mlsynth_cd/README.md`.
